packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-03 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

EXPOSURE STATEMENT
No proposed identification of this item was present in my context before reading.
My context did contain general project notes (an index mentioning a fragment
project) but nothing about these leaves. The leaf itself carries a printed running
title (see below); I transcribe it as visible text and draw no conclusion from it.
I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..012 in this packet. I did not read
packet.json, use the web, or search. One directory listing of the three packet
directories was made to learn the image filenames (it showed packet.json's name
only). Nothing else beyond the rules.

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image only)

Observation: this is PRINTED text (roman type with long s, ligatures ct/st,
tildes for nasal abbreviation), not handwriting. Language: French.

The packet shows four faces, in two physically different pieces:

(a) image-001 (overview; tiles 002, 003) and image-004 (overview; tiles 005, 006):
    two faces of one small torn paper scrap, upright, single column, large type.
    A running title in spaced small capitals stands at the top of each face.
    10-11 lines survive per face; left and right edges torn, so most lines lack
    beginning and/or end. Bottom line of each face is cut through horizontally.
    A crease/tear runs diagonally through the upper part. Show-through from the
    other face is visible. No rubrics, initials, underlining or glosses.

(b) image-007 (overview; tiles 008, 009) and image-010 (overview; tiles 011, 012):
    two faces of a horizontal strip, upright, smaller type than (a). Each face
    shows two blocks of text side by side separated by a wide blank gutter. Each
    block ends with its own catchword, and on image-010 the right block has a
    signature mark "B 3" in the foot line. Observation: two blocks, each with its
    own catchword. Tentative interpretation: these are the lower parts of two
    separate pages lying side by side on one sheet, not two columns of one page;
    reading order between the two blocks is therefore NOT established by the
    image. A stained vertical fold/stub with a hole runs along one outer edge
    (left on 007, right on 010). Wide blank lower margin, stained along the
    bottom. Faint brownish offset or marks in the gutter of image-007. No
    rubrics, enlarged initials, underlining, marginal or interlinear glosses.

Whether piece (a) and piece (b) come from the same book is not determinable from
the images; the type sizes differ.

2. SPANS SELECTED
All visible text on all four faces was read (the text is short). Nothing was left
unread except letters lost at torn edges. Overview and tile readings agree.

Conventions: long s is rendered as s; u/v and i/j kept as printed; tildes kept
(ã, õ, ẽ) with expansion in parentheses; [..] = letters lost at a torn edge;
"?" follows an uncertain reading. Line numbers count printed lines from the top
of the named image, running title included.

3. TRANSCRIPTION

--- Face A1: image-001 (overview); tile image-002 repeats lines 1-5 (and the
    tops of line 6); tile image-003 repeats lines 5-11 (with the feet of line 4
    at its top). These are overlaps, not additional text. ---

image-001 l.1   (running title, spaced small capitals)  SERMON DE
image-001 l.2   [..]ne. En ceste maniere Ab[..]
image-001 l.3   [..]ut agreable à Dieu ; car pou[..]
image-001 l.4   [..]laire, il ne craignit point de
image-001 l.5   [..]dre son fils, & ne refusa de c[..]
image-001 l.6   [..]mettre vn parricide. Toy qu[..]
image-001 l.7   veux perdre ton fils par la loy
image-001 l.8   condition de la nature, que fero[..]
image-001 l.9   [..] si? on te commandoit de le tuer
image-001 l.10  La crainte de? Dieu & la foy te doi[..]
image-001 l.11  [only the tops of letters survive, cut through by the lower tear;
                 unreadable]

Notes: l.1 second letter of SERMON is damaged by the crease (reads S.RMON; E
taken as probable). l.2 first surviving letters "ne." or "me." before the full
stop. l.3 "ut" could be "[..]it"/"[..]ut". l.5 first letters read "dre" (ascender
of d partly lost; "lre" as printed-looking shape). l.7 "loy" is followed by torn
edge; a further letter may be lost. l.9 the start is damaged by a tear and a
lifted flap: "si" is probable, preceded by lost letters. l.10 "de" is partly
abraded; initial "La" has its L partly lost.

--- Face A2: image-004 (overview); tile image-005 repeats lines 1-5 (tops of
    line 6); tile image-006 repeats lines 5-11. Overlaps only. ---

image-004 l.1   (running title, spaced small capitals)  S. CYPRIAN.
image-004 l.2   [..]stes ont tousiours esté pou[..]
image-004 l.3   & munis de ceste patience
image-004 l.4   postres pareillement ont tenu?
image-004 l.5   doctrine de la loy du Sei-
image-004 l.6   [..]r, de ne murmurer point és
image-004 l.7   [..]ersitez , mais supporter con-
image-004 l.8   [..]mment & patiemment tout ce
image-004 l.9   [..]ui leur aduiendra, comme il e[..]
image-004 l.10  [..]scrit, Le sacrifice à Dieu c'est vn
image-004 l.11  [..]sprit troubl[..]   (lower half of the line cut away)

Notes: l.2 "tousiours" - the "io" is deformed by the crease. l.3 "ceste" has its
"e" damaged by the crease. l.4 last letter at the torn edge, "tenu" probable.
l.5 the line appears to begin at "doctrine" with a blank or lost space before it.
l.6 first surviving letter looks like "r" preceded by a trace (possibly "[..]ur").
l.9 after "comme il" one or two damaged letters ("e[st]"? not confirmed).
l.11 only upper halves of letters; "troubl" probable, ending lost.
The beginnings of lines 3-5 may be complete or may have lost one or two letters
at the left tear; l.4 "postres" looks like the continuation of a word begun on
the previous line.

--- Face B1: image-007 (overview). Left block = tile image-008; right block =
    tile image-009. Image-008 also shows the first two or three letters of each
    right-block line; that is overlap. ---

LEFT BLOCK
image-008 l.1   [..]is? encourent ensemble
image-008 l.2   [..]esme ruine & desolation par
image-008 l.3   la prise d'icelle. Quãd (Quand) les nues clai-
image-008 l.4   res & serenes tiennent les eaux du
image-008 l.5   Ciel suspendues, la secheresse est
image-008 l.6   commune à tous. Et quand les ro-
image-008 l.7   chers brisent le vaisseau, le naufra-
image-008 l.8   ge est sans exception cõmun (commun) à tous
image-008 l.9   ceux, qui sont en mesme nauire.
image-008 l.10  Ne plus ny moins aussi la douleur
image-008 l.11  des yeux, l'ardeur des fieures, & la
image-008 l.12  debilitation de tous les membres
image-008 l.13  (catchword, right-aligned)  nous

Notes: l.1 the left part is torn away; "is" before "encourent" is the end of a
lost word. l.2 first letter(s) lost; "[m]esme" probable from the surviving
"eſme". Initial letters of ll.4, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12 are partly hidden by the stained
fold but readable as given (l.7 "c" and l.8 "g" are the least secure).

RIGHT BLOCK
image-009 l.1   [..]. Dieu ne m[..]      (upper half of the line torn away)
image-009 l.2   point le cœur contrict & humilié.
image-009 l.3   Et ailleurs le sainct Esprit nous ad-
image-009 l.4   monneste par Moyse en disant, Le
image-009 l.5   Seigneur ton Dieu t'affligera &
image-009 l.6   t'enuoyera la famine, & lors sera
image-009 l.7   connu & manifesté en toy, si tu au-
image-009 l.8   ras bien gardé ses cõmandemens, (commandemens)
image-009 l.9   ou non. Et derechef, Le Seigneur
image-009 l.10  vostre Dieu vous tente, à fin qu'il
image-009 l.11  sçache, si vous aimez Dieu de tout
image-009 l.12  vostre cœur & de toute vostre
image-009 l.13  (catchword, right-aligned)  ame.

Notes: l.1 only lower parts of letters; "Dieu ne" is secure, the word after it
begins with m or n and is lost. l.6 the word is printed "t'enuoyera" (the second
vowel looks like a turned or worn letter, u/n).

--- Face B2: image-010 (overview). Left block = tile image-011; right block =
    tile image-012. Image-012 also shows the last letters of the left-block
    lines; that is overlap. ---

LEFT BLOCK
image-011 l.1   prest & d[..]p?[..]      (lower half of the line torn away)
image-011 l.2   choses: soit que tu viennes à per-
image-011 l.3   dre tes biens, soit que tu sois tour-
image-011 l.4   menté en tes membres par longues
image-011 l.5   & cruelles maladies, soit qu'il t'ad-
image-011 l.6   uienne vne triste & funeste separa-
image-011 l.7   tion d'auec ta femme, tes enfans &
image-011 l.8   tes plus chers amis, que ces choses
image-011 l.9   ne te soient point comme scanda-
image-011 l.10  les, ains comme cõbats; (combats) & qu'elles
image-011 l.11  n'affoiblissẽt (affoiblissent) point la foy du Chre-
image-011 l.12  stien, mais que plustost elles mon-
image-011 l.13  (catchword, right-aligned)  strent

Notes: l.1 after "&" the tops of about three letters, the first "d" and a
descender further on. l.2 "choses" - the h is broken and looks like "cnoses";
"que" is printed with a letter resembling "qne" (worn or turned u).

RIGHT BLOCK
image-012 l.1   mais, que y a-il en ce m?[..]
image-012 l.2   ne nous soit commun auec
image-012 l.3   les hommes, tant que nous partici-
image-012 l.4   pons encores à ceste chair, selon
image-012 l.5   la loy de nostre premiere natiuité[punctuation hidden in fold]
image-012 l.6   Tandis que nous viuons icy nous
image-012 l.7   sommes conioints auec le genre
image-012 l.8   humain par la conformité d'vne?
image-012 l.9   mesme chair, mais nous en som-
image-012 l.10  mes separez d'esprit. Parquoy, ius-
image-012 l.11  qu'à ce que ce corps corruptible
image-012 l.12  veste l'incorruption, & que ceste
image-012 l.13  (foot line)  B 3   [signature mark]        (catchword)  mor-

Notes: l.1 the last visible letter is the left part of m or n; the rest of the
line is torn off. l.2 the line may have lost a word after "auec" at the torn
edge. Line ends of ll.3-12 run into the stained fold: "partici-", "selon",
"nous", "genre", "d'vne", "som-", "ius-", "ceste" are read through the stain;
the final letter of l.8 is the least secure (hole in the paper beside it).
l.12 "veste" is the complete first word as printed (no letter lost before it).

4. LIMITATIONS
- Piece (a): both faces lack line beginnings and/or ends on almost every line,
  and the last line of each face is cut through. No complete sentence survives.
  Which face is recto and which verso is not determinable from the images. The
  running title reads SERMON DE on one face and S. CYPRIAN. on the other; I have
  not used it to supply any text.
- Piece (b): the two blocks on each face each end with a catchword, so they are
  probably the feet of two different pages. I give them left then right as seen,
  without claiming they are consecutive. The top line of each block is partly
  torn away. Text above these 12-line feet is lost.
- A wider view is not needed; all surviving print is covered by the tiles. The
  only gains would come from raking light on the stained fold (image-012 line
  ends) and on the abraded last lines of piece (a).
- This is an unverified image reading.
